deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page (284) ends a trigonometric identity of a different kind. This page opens a new topic, 'Determinanten'. The next page (286) contains the three theorems announced at the foot of this page.

(1) 2x2 case. For the array
  α β
  γ δ
the determinant is defined as αδ − βγ. In index notation the entry in column i and row j is written (ij), so the first digit is the column and the second the row. The array is then
  (00) (10)
  (01) (11)
and its determinant is (00)(11) − (10)(01). This is abbreviated (01.01): the column indices, then the row indices.

(2) 3x3 case. Write a_{ij} = (ij), column i, row j. The determinant
(012,012) = (00)(11)(22) + (10)(21)(02) + (20)(01)(12) − (10)(01)(22) − (21)(12)(00) − (02)(20)(11).
In modern terms this is the Leibniz sum Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j a_{σ(j),j}.
- The three positive terms correspond to the identity and the two 3-cycles.
- The three negative terms correspond to the three transpositions.

(3) Minors of a larger matrix. If the 3x3 array is part of an n x n system, label the columns a,b,c and the rows α,β,γ. The entries are (aα), (bα), ... and
(abc, αβγ) = (aα)(bβ)(cγ) + (bα)(cβ)(aγ) + (cα)(aβ)(bγ) − (bα)(aβ)(cγ) − (cβ)(bγ)(aα) − (aγ)(cα)(bβ).
The substitution a,b,c → 0,1,2 and α,β,γ → 0,1,2 reproduces formula (2) term for term. So (abc, αβγ) is the minor with column set {a,b,c} and row set {α,β,γ}. The text remarks that this notation makes the meaning of the position of the indices clear.

(4) General n x n case. Here the determinant has 1·2·3···n = n! terms, half with + and half with −.

(5) Announcement of three theorems, stated for simplicity for 5x5 but 'easily generalised'. They appear on the next page:
- I. Laplace (cofactor) expansion along the last row:
  (01234,01234) = (0123,0123)(44) − (0124,0123)(34) + (0134,0123)(24) − (0234,0123)(14) + (1234,0123)(04).
- II. The Desnanot–Jacobi (Sylvester / Dodgson condensation) identity:
  (01234,01234)(234,234) = (0234,0234)(1234,1234) − (0234,1234)(1234,0234).
- III. A further minor relation, transcribed incompletely.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The 2x2 and 3x3 expansions have correct signs, and the general (abc,αβγ) formula matches the numeric 3x3 formula term by term.
The count 'n! terms, half + and half −' holds for n ≥ 2. Linear dependence among terms is not an issue for generic entries.
Next page: Theorems I and II as transcribed are correct. Theorem III is transcribed incompletely (no '=' sign, one term marked [?]), so it cannot be verified as written.

deep.surprise_reason: This page itself contains only definitions and notation for determinants and minors, which is routine material. Two things are mildly notable. First, the German term 'Determinante' is used in the modern n x n sense, and Gauss's own published 'determinans' (Disquisitiones, 1801) referred to the discriminant of quadratic forms. Second, the announced theorems on the next page include the Desnanot–Jacobi identity. If the sheet really dates from around 1809, it would predate Cauchy 1812 and Desnanot 1819. However, the date is uncertain: the bundle label is not a dating of the page, and the terminology and notation resemble post-Cauchy/Jacobi usage. The hand also may not be Gauss's own; it could be a copy. Hence only a modest score.
